result.description:
A rewarding opportunity has emerged for a dedicated Clinical Pharmacist to join a vibrant healthcare team in the Northern Territory. This locum placement is set within a dynamic public hospital environment, offering a unique chance to provide essential clinical services to a diverse patient population while experiencing the rich cultural heritage and breathtaking landscapes of Australia’s Top End. 

 The successful candidate will be responsible for providing high-level clinical pharmacy services, including medication reviews, ward-based clinical support, and multidisciplinary collaboration. The contract is scheduled to commence on 04/05/2026 for an initial duration of 8 weeks. To be considered, candidates must demonstrate proficiency with the Merlin medication system. Compliance is paramount; all applicants must provide an Australian Standard competency set, a valid Ochre Card (Working with Children Clearance), and a National Police Check (NPC/CHC/CRC) issued within the last six months by an authorized Australian authority. Completed Vaccination Preparedness Declaration (VPD) forms are also required prior to commencement. 

 This role offers highly competitive locum rates, depending on experience. In addition to the attractive hourly pay, the placement includes comprehensive support such as subsidised or provided accommodation and travel assistance to help you settle into the Territory. 

 Working in the Northern Territory is more than just a job; it is a lifestyle adventure. Beyond the clinical setting, locums can enjoy a relaxed tropical pace of life, world-class fishing, and weekend excursions to iconic destinations like Litchfield and Kakadu National Parks. Whether you are exploring the bustling night markets of Darwin or the red sands of the desert, the Territory offers a work-life balance that is difficult to match elsewhere in Australia. Concord Emergency Department is seeking motivated ACEM Advanced Trainees (AT) to develop a unique skillset on our team.

The Hospital

Concord Repatriation General Hospital is proud of its healthcare service excellence and leadership in clinical care. Concord is part of a network of hospitals and healthcare services within Sydney Local Health District and offers a comprehensive range of specialty and sub-specialty services in the inner-western suburbs of Sydney.

Concord Hospital is committed to ensuring the community has equitable access to high quality patient-centred care that is timely, evidence-based, culturally appropriate and efficient. The hospital provides this care in partnership with highly skilled and committed staff.

The Department of Emergency Medicine

The Emergency department has 2 resus bays, 16 acute beds, a rapid access and fast track area and a new 5-bed ED short stay unit due for completion in late 2026. A high-end CT scanner has been installed adjacent to the resuscitation bays with a co-located radiology department.

Our department is a receiving centre for major burns, a primary PTCA centre for STEMI and is an acute stroke service referral centre. Our patient population is a cohort with complex medical conditions and high acuity presentations and a small proportion of paediatric attendances.

Concord ED is a major referral site and is accredited for 24 months of advanced ED training with Australasian College of Emergency Medicine (ACEM). We provide opportunities to get involved in research and quality assurance activities and encourage consolidating the practice of evidence-based medicine.

The role

As an ED AT you will be part of the dynamic team providing emergency care under the guidance of Emergency Consultants. We will provide you with the opportunity to develop a broad range of clinical skills in a well-supported environment to progress in your career in emergency medicine focussed on medical complexity and high acuity presentations.

Concord ED has an established program for professional development and structured education. We pride ourselves on providing you with a supportive educational environment and flexibility to meet your professional development needs and training goals. This includes:

 Weekly ED registrar teaching (5-hours paid protected time)

 Rotations to develop specialised skills in anaesthetics, intensive care, trauma at Royal Prince Alfred Hospital, paediatrics (ED or ward) at Canterbury Hospital as well as ultrasound, burns and Geriatric Emergency Medicine (GEM) special skills terms

 Dedicated fellowship examination preparation program delivered by an enthusiastic team of consultants.

 Candidate or participant role in Concord ED bi-annual trial OSCE

 Point of Care Ultrasound education

 Clinical audit opportunities to develop a non-clinical portfolio

 Mentorship and career development support to join specialty training programs

 Bedside teaching program including procedural skills accreditation for sedation and central access

 In-situ interprofessional simulation program

 ACEM Associateship training program in Emergency Medicine as an alternative to ACEM training.

 A supportive, collegiate, and diverse work environment

 Convenient location near transport facilities with onsite parking available.

 Salary packaging and fitness passport for eligible staff including utilising SLHD gym facilities

 Wellbeing, advocacy, mentorship, and support opportunities exclusively for medical staff through SLHDs multifaceted workplace program MDOK

 Burns (special skills term)

This unique ACEM accredited rotation consists of a 0.5 Burns and a 0.5 ED component over a 6-month term. It is the only one of its kind in Australia! The ED burns registrar is integrated into the burns team and involved in all aspects of burns care. This provides opportunity to develop special clinical skills, teaching and quality improvement work.

Ultrasound (special skills term)

This rotation enables consolidation of advanced ultrasound skills under the guidance of dedicated supervisors. It is made up of a 0.5 ultrasound and a 0.5 ED component over a 6-month term. Trainees will be supported to accomplish accreditation in multiple CCU units and integrate ultrasound skills in practice.

Anaesthetics and ICU

There are 3-month terms available at CRGH for ICU and anaesthetics that would allow an advanced trainee to satisfy part of the critical care component of FACEM training.

Full-Time: Immediate start
Reports to: Manager
Job Title: Beef Cattle Farm Worker
Salary range: $80,000 - $100,000 + Superannuation & other – depending on skill level
Job Closure date: 30 days

About The Role
On behalf of our client, a progressive and data-driven Angus seed stock operation in the Great Southern region, we are seeking a dedicated and skilled Beef Cattle Farm Worker. This is not just a farmhand role; it is an opportunity to contribute to a strategic breeding program focused on excellence.
Our client has meticulously built a renowned breeding herd over the past decade, with a core philosophy of combining superior genetics with functional, structurally sound cattle. They are committed to advancing their herd through rigorous data-driven selection and a steadfast focus on traits that deliver real profitability and reliability for their commercial bull customers.
We are looking for an individual who is passionate about modern, sustainable beef production and possesses a keen eye for animal detail. The successful candidate will play a hands-on role in the daily care and strategic management of this high-value stud herd, ensuring the highest standards of animal welfare, pasture health, and operational efficiency are maintained.

Key Responsibilities & Duties:
Livestock Care & Health Management
• Conduct daily inspections of cattle to monitor health, behaviour, and well-being, promptly reporting any signs of illness, injury, or distress.
• Feed and water management: Ensure cattle receive balanced nutrition by distributing feed, maintaining feeding schedules, and keeping water troughs clean and functional.
• Assist with veterinary procedures, including vaccinations, drenching, tagging, and administering medications under supervision.
• Support calving operations, assisting with birthing when necessary and ensuring newborn calves receive proper care.
• Assist in breeding programs, including heat detection, artificial insemination (if applicable), and record-keeping.

Grazing & Pasture Management
• Rotational grazing: Move cattle between paddocks to optimize pasture usage, prevent overgrazing, and promote forage regrowth.
• Monitor pasture conditions, identifying weed infestations, soil erosion, or fencing issues that may affect livestock movement.
• Assist in silage/hay production (if applicable), including cutting, baling, and storage for winter feed.

Farm Maintenance & Equipment Operation
• Perform routine repairs on fences, gates, cattle yards, and handling facilities to ensure structural integrity and livestock safety.
• Maintain and clean feeding systems, water pumps, and irrigation equipment to prevent blockages or malfunctions.
• Operate farm machinery (tractors, ATVs, feed mixers, etc.) for feeding, spraying, or pasture maintenance (training provided if needed).
• Assist with weed and pest control to maintain a safe and productive grazing environment.

Cattle Handling & Movement
• Safely mustering, drafting, and sorting cattle using low-stress handling techniques.
• Assist with loading/unloading livestock for transport, sales, or processing, ensuring compliance with animal welfare standards.
• Participate in branding, tagging, and weighing operations as part of herd management.

Record-Keeping & Compliance
• Maintain accurate livestock records, including health treatments, breeding, and weight data.
• Follow biosecurity protocols to prevent disease spread between livestock or properties.
• Adhere to workplace health and safety regulations, including safe chemical handling and machinery use.

Requirements & Qualifications:
• Minimum 1 year of experience in beef cattle farming, livestock handling, or a related agricultural role.
• Strong animal husbandry skills with an understanding of cattle behaviour, nutrition, and health needs.
• Farm machinery experience (tractors, quad bikes, feed wagons) is highly desirable.
• Basic mechanical skills for minor repairs and maintenance of farm infrastructure.
• Valid driver’s license (truck or tractor license is a plus).
• Flexibility to work early mornings, weekends, and public holidays as required by seasonal demands.
• Team player with strong communication skills and the ability to follow instructions.
• Certification in Livestock Production, Agriculture, or Animal Science if preferable but not required.

How to Apply:
Interested candidates should submit a resume and brief cover letter outlining their experience and suitability for the role.

Please note: We are acting as recruitment agents on behalf of our client. Employer details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.
